priority_review.title: Self-image as working self-description
priority_review.original_common_misreading: Treating a conceptual or anecdotal explanation as a universal causal law, without evaluating context, skills or competing explanations.
priority_review.proposed_specific_caution_NOT_CANONICAL: The working self-description may influence choices, but it does not control every action; resources, environment and prior learning also matter.

rationale_from_inherited_record.thesis: An accumulated working picture of what kind of person one is can influence what one attempts and expects.
rationale_from_inherited_record.conditions_and_limits: The text claims absolute control over all actions; do not present that universal assertion as an established law.
rationale_from_inherited_record.alternative_explanation: Expectancies, environment, available resources, habitual action and interpersonal feedback all shape behavior; no single self-image variable explains every outcome.

priority_review.title: Surgery, appearance and subjective identity
priority_review.original_common_misreading: Treating a conceptual or anecdotal explanation as a universal causal law, without evaluating context, skills or competing explanations.
priority_review.proposed_specific_caution_NOT_CANONICAL: An altered appearance does not reliably produce an altered self-image; neither surgery nor self-reflection is a stand-alone treatment for body-image distress.

rationale_from_inherited_record.thesis: An external cosmetic change does not reliably produce a corresponding change in how someone perceives or values themself.
rationale_from_inherited_record.conditions_and_limits: Never suggest cosmetic surgery or self-image exercises alone treat body-dysmorphic distress.
rationale_from_inherited_record.alternative_explanation: Social treatment, reduced stigma, expectation and broader circumstances may account for some changes.

priority_review.title: Imagination as goal picture

priority_review.proposed_specific_caution_NOT_CANONICAL: Visualizing an event is not equivalent to actually performing it; claims that the nervous system makes no distinction are overstated.

priority_review.title: Hypnosis and belief-based behavior
priority_review.original_common_misreading: Treating a conceptual or anecdotal explanation as a universal causal law, without evaluating context, skills or competing explanations.
priority_review.proposed_specific_caution_NOT_CANONICAL: Hypnosis anecdotes do not establish reliable surgical pain control; suggestions and attention cannot replace anesthesia or clinical care.

rationale_from_inherited_record.thesis: The chapter invokes Theodore Barber to argue that accepted suggestions can affect performance and behavior.
rationale_from_inherited_record.conditions_and_limits: Claims of surgery without anesthesia or effortless recovery need clinical qualification; never substitute self-hypnosis for care.
rationale_from_inherited_record.alternative_explanation: Expectancy, suggestion, attention and context may affect outcomes, depending on the task.

priority_review.proposed_specific_caution_NOT_CANONICAL: Relief of perceived stress or pain is not evidence of faster tissue repair; never use imagery as a substitute for medical treatment.

priority_review.title: Mental-state medical claims require boundaries
priority_review.original_common_misreading: Treating the book’s metaphor, attributed example or categorical advice as established science or a guarantee.
priority_review.proposed_specific_caution_NOT_CANONICAL: A positive mood must not be portrayed as the sole cause of good health or a cure for illness; medical treatment and other factors matter.

rationale_from_inherited_record.conditions_and_limits: Claims that happiness cures illness or is the only cure are unsupported and dangerous to repeat as medical guidance.
